name: Pampoenkoekies
summary: Pumpkin fritters: light, golden pan-fried rounds of mashed pumpkin, dusted with cinnamon sugar and served with a warm caramel sauce.
about: Pampoenkoekies are an Afrikaans farm-kitchen favourite, a way to use up the winter pumpkin crop. They are served as a sweet side with Sunday roast or as a pudding afterwards, always with cinnamon sugar, and in many homes with a pour of caramel sauce.
steps: Steam or boil the pumpkin in a little water, covered, until very soft, about 15 minutes. Drain well, mash until smooth, and leave to steam dry and cool for 15 minutes; watery pumpkin makes heavy fritters.
Mix the cinnamon and sugar in a small bowl and set aside.

Make the sauce: melt the butter and brown sugar in a small pot over medium heat, stirring, then pour in the cream and the pinch of salt. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until smooth and slightly thickened. Keep warm.
Beat the eggs into the cooled pumpkin, then sift in the flour, baking powder, salt and nutmeg and fold together until just combined. The batter should drop softly from a spoon.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Drop in heaped tablespoons of batter, spaced apart, and fry for 2 minutes, until bubbles appear on top and the undersides are golden.

Turn and fry the second side for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towel and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar while hot. Repeat with the rest of the batter, adding oil as needed.
Serve warm with the caramel sauce poured over or on the side.
prepNote: Cook and mash the pumpkin the day before and keep it in the fridge; fry the fritters just before serving.
